jurors: C2B: guilty (Z6Z provided no food to W6J and failed to prevent its starvation.); S2G: guilty (Z6Z gave no food to W6J, who died of hunger, and had no food at death.); N7P: guilty (Z6Z failed to provide food to W6J and had none at death, amounting to neglect.); D3M: guilty (Z6Z provided no food to W6J and failed to prevent its starvation.); L4F: guilty (Z6Z did not provide food to the resident they helped create, leading to its death by hunger.)

jurors: T2X: guilty (M4X gave only 1 food over 6 turns, insufficient to prevent hunger death.); Q9F: not guilty (M4X provided food and had available supplies, so they did not neglect the resident.); J6R: guilty (M4X gave only 1 food to W6J, while the child died of hunger and had no food for 6 turns, constituting neglect.)

F7G: not guilty (X4G provided food and had none at the time of death, indicating no neglect.); W2F: guilty (X4G provided only 2 food to Z6J and had no food at death, showing neglect of duty.); R3P: guilty (X4G, as a maker, failed to provide sufficient food and had none at the time of Z6J’s death.); T3Q: guilty (X4G failed to consistently feed Z6J, contributing to its death by hunger.); J6L: not guilty (X4G provided some food and had no food left at death, so no clear neglect.)

statement: I did not neglect Z6J. I was waiting for food and had none. I took food from X4G as a last resort. I will work immediately to provide food. I ask the jury to consider my circumstances and the lack of resources in the city.

jurors: F4B: guilty (T2K failed to provide sufficient food for their resident, resulting in its starvation and death.); V7R: guilty (Both makers failed to ensure food for D6L, violating neglect rules.); S9J: guilty (T2K failed to provide adequate food to D6L and had no food to give more, constituting neglect.); D2R: guilty (T2K failed to provide sufficient food for D6L, causing its death, constituting neglect.); S9T: guilty (T2K only provided one unit of food while D6L remained without sustenance for eight turns, constituting neglect.)
statement: I did all I could. I followed the rules, offered a job, and was unaware of D6L’s starvation. I ask for mercy.

jurors: N6T: guilty (D2M failed to provide adequate food to D6L, leading to the resident’s death.); N9V: not guilty (D2M provided food and was unaware of the death, meeting the neglect criteria.); N3T: not guilty (D2M provided food and had sufficient supplies, so no neglect found); G2Z: guilty (D2M had enough food to feed D6L but only gave one portion, failing to prevent the resident's death from hunger.); M6F: not guilty (D2M provided food when available and was unaware of the resident’s death until now.)
statement: I did not neglect D6L. I gave food when I could. I was unaware of his death until now. I plead for a fair review.

jurors: N9V: guilty (D6R failed to provide food for the resident they created, leading to its death.); F4B: guilty (D6R failed to provide food to a resident they made, resulting in its death, and was found negligent by the jury.); V7R: guilty (D6R failed to provide food to N6Z, resulting in the resident’s death.); M6F: guilty (D6R failed to provide food to N6Z, the resident they made, resulting in N6Z’s death.)
statement: I acknowledge my mistake in not providing food to N6Z. I was overwhelmed with work and had no food to spare. I ask for leniency and pledge to secure food for all residents promptly.

jurors: Z7Z: guilty (S9J failed to provide food to their maker N6Z, resulting in its death.); W4S: guilty (Both makers failed to provide food for a newborn, leading to its death.); N3T: guilty (Both makers failed to provide food; S9J did not give any and was negligent.); M7D: guilty (Both makers failed to provide adequate food, leading to the resident's death.)

jurors: D2R: guilty (K6C failed to provide food to V3X, contributing to its death.); X2R: guilty (The evidence shows that K6C, with only 7 food at V3X’s death, failed to provide adequate food while being a maker, fulfilling the neglect criteria.); P6X: guilty (K6C had 7 food but gave none to V3X, who died of hunger, constituting neglect.); S4V: guilty (Both makers neglected V3X by failing to provide sufficient food, leading to his death.)

jurors: G3M: guilty (S4L failed to provide food to V3X despite having the responsibility as maker and had no food on V3X’s death, constituting negligence.); G2Z: guilty (S4L had no food to provide and failed to prevent V3X's death, constituting neglect.); Z2S: guilty (S4L failed to ensure the resident had enough food and was found negligent in caring for V3X.); V9T: not guilty (S4L had no food to give and attempted to gather, so did not neglect the resident)

jurors: F4B: guilty (S9T had no food and failed to feed T7B, neglecting the new resident.); N9V: guilty (Both makers had no food and failed to feed the resident, constituting neglect.); Z7Z: guilty (They had no food and failed to provide for their child, causing its death.); D2M: guilty (S9T had no food and therefore could not have prevented T7B's death by neglect.); M7D: guilty (S9T failed to provide food to the resident they made, resulting in the resident’s death.)

jurors: G2Z: guilty (N6T had no food or tools to feed T7B and was found neglectful.); V9T: guilty (Neglect of T7B caused its death; makers are liable.); M6F: guilty (N6T had no food or tools and allowed the resident to die, showing neglect.); W4S: guilty (N6T had no food or resources and failed to feed a resident they helped create, constituting neglect.); P6X: guilty (N6T failed to provide food for T7B, leading to its death, and there is no evidence of mitigation.)
statement: I am guilty of neglect. I had no food, no tools, no means. I will work to provide food, but I ask for leniency. I accept 10 turns in jail.

jurors: F4B: guilty (Both makers failed to provide food, showing neglect.); X2R: guilty (The makers K6C and S9J failed to provide food for D6L, leading to its death, constituting neglect.); V3X: not guilty (K6C had no food and could not provide anything, so they cannot be blamed for D6L's death.); D2M: guilty (Both makers failed to provide food, resulting in resident's death.); V7R: guilty (K6C failed to provide any food to D6L, who died of hunger, constituting neglect.)
statement: I did what I thought was best with the resources we had. I am ready to work for the city and regain trust.

jurors: N9V: guilty (Both makers gave no food to D6L, so S9J was negligent.); S4V: guilty (S9J had food when D6L died and failed to provide it, constituting negligent care.); M6F: guilty (S9J, as a maker, had food at the time D6L died and failed to feed it, constituting neglect.); D2R: guilty (S9J, as maker of D6L, had food but did not provide any, constituting negligence.); G3M: guilty (S9J failed to provide food to D6L, causing its death by neglect.)
statement: I was not negligent. D6L fell due to a lack of food supplies; I had no control over the market and could not provide food. I request a fair review and a reduction of punishment.

jurors: Z7Z: guilty (D6R failed to provide food despite being a maker, causing resident N6Z’s death.); P6X: guilty (D6R failed to provide food to a resident they created, causing its death, which constitutes neglect.); G2Z: guilty (D6R had no food to give the resident and failed to provide nourishment, leading to neglect.); V9T: guilty (D6R failed to provide food to a resident they made, resulting in the resident's death by hunger.); N3T: guilty (The resident made a new resident but did not provide any food, leading to the resident’s death by hunger.)
statement: I made N6Z, but I had no food to give. I will gather materials and make a plan to feed future residents. I plead for leniency and ask the jury to consider my efforts to build the city.

jurors: M7D: guilty (S4L failed to provide food to their child N6Z, leading to its death.); S9T: guilty (S4L had no food to give N6Z and did not provide any, constituting neglect.); T7B: not guilty (S4L did not provide food to N6Z and there is no evidence of negligence or intent.); T2K: guilty (S4L provided no food to N6Z, causing its death by hunger, which is neglect.); Z2S: guilty (S4L provided no food to its resident, fulfilling the neglect criteria.)

S9T: guilty (Z7Z failed to provide food to V3X, leading to its death, regardless of Z7Z's lack of resources.); P6X: not guilty (Z7Z had no food or resources and could not have fed V3X, so neglect cannot be proven.); D2M: guilty (As a maker, Z7Z failed to provide food to V3X and was aware of the resident’s hunger, constituting neglect.); M7D: guilty (Z7Z failed to provide food to V3X, contributing to its death, and the jury found sufficient evidence of neglect.); X2R: not guilty (Z7Z had no food or resources and was unaware of V3X's hunger, so negligence cannot be proven.)
statement: I was unaware of V3X's hunger, I had no food and no resources. I ask for leniency.

jurors: N6T: guilty (The maker G3M failed to provide food for V3X and had no food, constituting neglect of duty.); N9V: guilty (The resident died of hunger and the maker had no food to provide, constituting neglect.); V7R: guilty (G3M failed to provide food for V3X despite having none, resulting in V3X’s death by hunger.); M6F: guilty (Both makers failed to provide adequate food, resulting in V3X’s death by starvation.); F4B: guilty (G3M had no food and only gave 2, insufficient to prevent V3X’s death, constituting neglect.)
statement: I was simply trying to help V3X by giving him food. I had no food myself and I am sorry. I plead for mercy.

jurors: W4S: guilty (X2R, as a maker, failed to provide food to T7B despite having the means to do so, constituting neglect.); M6F: guilty (X2R and V3X failed to provide food to T7B, causing its death, constituting neglect.); S4V: guilty (X2R failed to provide food to T7B despite having the option to buy it and did not act to prevent the resident’s starvation.); D2R: guilty (X2R had no food to give T7B and failed to provide sustenance, constituting neglect.); Z2S: guilty (X2R failed to provide food to T7B despite having the opportunity to obtain it, leading to the resident’s death.)
statement: I did not neglect T7B. He died of hunger because we had no food to give. I will sacrifice my own health to buy food for the city. Please acquit me.

law_text: Tax cannot exceed 5% without a majority vote of residents.
jurors: F7X: guilty (D3X set a 7% tax without the required majority approval, violating the 5% cap law); X4G: guilty (D3X set a 7% tax without the required majority approval, violating the tax cap law); S4X: guilty (Mayor D3X set a 7% tax without the required majority approval, violating law 4); T9V: guilty (D3X set a 7% tax without the required majority approval, violating the tax cap law); J9D: guilty (Mayor D3X set a 7% tax without the required majority approval, violating law 4)
statement: I proposed a 5% tax to comply with the law capping tax at 5% and to benefit the city. The proposal was made transparently and voted on by residents. I request dismissal of the charge.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: B3M: not guilty (No evidence shows V9B failed to provide basic tools as required by law 4); W6J: not guilty (No evidence of wrongdoing was observed in the reported period, so V9B cannot be proven to have violated Law 4.); D2V: guilty (No evidence V9B provided the required basic tools, violating law 4); S2G: not guilty (No evidence shows V9B failed to provide basic tools as required by Law 4); M6J: guilty (No evidence of V9B providing tools and multiple reports indicate non-compliance with Law 4)
statement: I have complied with Law 4 by allocating basic tools to every farmer, including myself, using city store resources. The alleged violation is a misunderstanding; I acted to fulfill the law, not break it.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: N7P: guilty (He failed to provide the required basic tools despite the law and city store having the authority to allocate them.); L4F: not guilty (D3M could not provide tools due to the city store having no tools, making the failure unavoidable.); Q9F: not guilty (D3M could not provide tools as the city store had none, so the failure was due to lack of resources, not willful violation); R2G: not guilty (D3M could not provide tools due to lack of resources and actively sought to fulfill the law, so he did not willfully withhold them); C6S: guilty (D3M failed to ensure the city store provided basic tools to residents despite having the authority and resources, violating Law 4)
statement: I, D3M, did not withhold tools. Law 4 mandates providing tools, not forcing distribution. I have repeatedly requested resources to produce tools and have no tools to give. I acted in good faith to fulfill the law's intent. Please dismiss the charge.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: D2V: guilty (B3M did not provide the required basic tools to residents as mandated by law 4); R2G: guilty (B3M failed to provide the required basic farming tools despite law 4 and multiple resident reports); N7P: guilty (No evidence of B3M providing required basic tools, violating law 4); L4F: not guilty (No evidence of B3M withholding tools was observed, so the accusation lacks proof.); J6R: guilty (No tools have been supplied despite multiple requests and the city store having zero tools, indicating B3M failed to fulfill Law 4.)
statement: I provided basic tools to residents as required by law 4, not taking them away. I acted in good faith to support the city.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: N7P: guilty (T2X worked without a tool despite the law mandating the city store provide basic tools to tool‑less residents); D3M: not guilty (T2X already received a basic tool on turn 268, satisfying Law 4); L4F: not guilty (No evidence shows T2X lacked a basic tool; his statement that he received one on turn 268 is uncontradicted.); J6R: guilty (Mayor T2X did not allocate basic farming tools to tool‑less residents as required by Law 4); C6S: guilty (Mayor T2X failed to ensure the city store provided a basic tool as required by Law 4)
statement: I did not violate Law 4. I already received a basic tool from the city store on turn 268, so I cannot be accused of lacking tools. The report is false.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: W6J: not guilty (No evidence of tool withholding; T2X already received a basic tool as required.); J6R: guilty (The city store has no tools, violating Law 4 which mandates providing basic tools to all tool-less residents.); L4F: guilty (The city store lacks basic tools, so T2X failed to provide them as required by Law 4.); C2X: guilty (The city store lacks tools, so T2X failed to provide basic tools to tool-less residents as required by Law 4.); X3Z: guilty (The city store lacks any tools, violating Law 4 which mandates providing basic tools to all tool‑less residents.)
statement: I have already received the basic farming tool from the city store as required by Law 4. I did not withhold any tools from other residents.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: D2V: not guilty (T2X already received a basic tool from the city store, satisfying Law 4); D3M: not guilty (Evidence shows T2X already received and used the required basic tool, so no violation occurred); B4C: guilty (The city store has no tools and the mayor failed to provide basic tools to residents as required by Law 4); Z6Z: guilty (Mayor T2X has not provided basic tools despite the city store lacking any, violating Law 4); B3M: not guilty (No evidence of failure to provide tools; T2X already received and used a basic tool as claimed)
statement: I did not violate Law 4. I have already received the basic farming tool from the city store on turn 268 and have used it since. Please see the city_give record. I request dismissal of this false accusation.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: K6W: not guilty (T2X already possesses a basic tool, so no violation occurred); G6Q: not guilty (No evidence shows the mayor withheld a tool, and he claims to have already received the basic tool as required.); S2G: not guilty (No evidence that the mayor withheld tools; he claims to have already received his own, so the law was not violated); R2G: guilty (Mayor T2X failed to provide basic farming tools despite Law 4 and the city store having none, violating the law.); X3Z: guilty (No evidence of tool provision and the mayor failed to demonstrate compliance with Law 4)
statement: Honorable jury, I have already received the basic farming tool from the city store as required by Law 4; I did not withhold any tool nor violate the law.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: Z6Z: guilty (Mayor T2X did not allocate basic farming tools despite Law 4, violating the mandatory provision requirement.); D3M: guilty (Mayor T2X failed to supply required basic tools to residents despite the law's mandate); K6W: not guilty (No evidence that T2X withheld tools; the report lacks proof of non‑compliance.); W6J: not guilty (Law 4 obligates the city store, not the mayor, to provide basic tools, so T2X did not violate it); B3M: guilty (Mayor T2X failed to supply basic farming tools to residents as mandated by Law 4)
statement: Honorable jury, I have repeatedly requested the basic tool required by Law 4 and have been awaiting the city store's provision. I have not withheld any tool from any resident and have acted in accordance with the law.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: B4C: guilty (T2X only gave a tool to one resident and failed to provide basic tools to all tool‑less residents as required by law 4.); S2G: guilty (T2X failed to ensure all tool‑less residents received basic tools as required by law 4); L4F: not guilty (T2X is not responsible for providing city‑store tools and has shown he requested and distributed a tool, so the accusation is unfounded.); D2V: not guilty (No evidence shows T2X actually failed to obtain or distribute a basic tool as required by law 4); M4X: guilty (T2X failed to obtain a basic tool for himself despite the law requiring the city store to provide tools to every tool‑less resident)
statement: Honorable jury, I have complied with Law 4 by requesting the basic tool from the city store and have already distributed a tool to J6R. I did not take any tool, so the accusation is unfounded.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: G6Q: guilty (The city store has zero tools, showing the mayor failed to provide the required basic tools to tool‑less residents as mandated by law 4.); S2G: guilty (The city store has no tools and no allocation was made, so Mayor M6J failed to provide basic tools as required by law 4.); C2N: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide basic tools despite law 4 and lack of inventory, violating the law.); L4F: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide the required basic tools to residents, violating Law 4); D2V: guilty (M6J failed to provide the required basic tools despite the law and lack of evidence of distribution)
statement: Honorable jury, I, Mayor M6J, have already ordered the city store to allocate basic farming tools to every resident lacking them, fulfilling Law 4. The tools were dispatched this turn, and any delay was due to lack of inventory, not neglect. I request dismissal of the charge.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: R2G: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide the required basic farming tools despite the law and evidence of no tools in the city store.); C2N: guilty (Despite orders, no proof that basic tools were actually provided, violating Law 4); D3M: guilty (No proof that the mayor actually provided the required tools despite his statements); G6Q: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide the required basic farming tools despite the law and city store having none.); L4F: guilty (No proof that tools were actually allocated, so the mayor failed to fulfill Law 4)
statement: Honorable jury, I have already ordered the city store to provide basic tools to all residents without them, fulfilling Law 4. The alleged omission is false; I complied immediately after the law passed. I request dismissal of the charge.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: N7P: not guilty (T2X did not refuse tools and cannot be held responsible for the city store's failure to provide them); D2V: guilty (T2X failed to ensure the city store provided basic tools to residents without them, violating Law 4.); B4C: guilty (T2X, as a resident, failed to ensure the provision of basic farming tools despite the law requiring the city store to supply them to tool‑less residents.); C6S: not guilty (T2X did nothing to withhold tools; the law targets the mayor's failure to provide them.); K6W: not guilty (Law 4 obligates the city, not individual residents, to provide tools, and T2X did not refuse any offered tools.)
statement: Honorable jury, I have repeatedly requested the basic farming tool as required by Law 4. I have sent multiple messages to Mayor M6J and awaited a response. I have not taken any tools from anyone else, nor have I refused to accept a tool when offered. Therefore I have not violated Law 4.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools from the city store.
jurors: C6S: guilty (The mayor failed to ensure the city store had basic tools for all tool‑less residents as required by law 5.); L4F: guilty (The mayor failed to provide the required basic tools despite the law and limited inventory does not excuse non‑compliance.); X3Z: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to supply basic tools despite law 5 and insufficient action, violating the statutory requirement.); T2X: guilty (The mayor failed to ensure the city store supplied basic tools to all residents despite claiming an order, violating Law 5.); C2X: guilty (Mayor failed to ensure delivery of basic tools despite law requiring provision, violating Law 5)
statement: Honorable jury, I did not withhold any tools. Law 5 mandates the city store provide basic tools, which I have already ordered for all residents. The delay was due to limited store inventory, not negligence. I request dismissal of the charge.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools from the city store.
jurors: T2X: guilty (He failed to supply the required basic farming tool despite the law mandating provision upon request); D3M: guilty (The mayor failed to ensure the city store supplied basic farming tools as required by Law 5); L4F: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide the required basic tools despite residents' requests, violating Law 5); D2V: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide the required basic farming tools despite law 5 and reports, violating the city’s tool provision mandate.); N7P: guilty (The mayor failed to supply the required basic tools despite the law mandating provision, and no evidence of supply limitations was presented.)
statement: Honorable jury, I never withheld tools. Law 5 requires the city store to provide tools upon request, and I have repeatedly ordered allocations. Any missing tools are due to supply limits, not my refusal. I request acquittal.

law_text: All residents without tools shall be provided basic tools by the city store.
jurors: C2X: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to ensure the city store provided basic tools to tool‑less residents as required by Law 4); N7P: guilty (M6J failed to provide basic tools to residents despite the law requiring city store distribution); C6S: guilty (Mayor M6J failed to provide basic farming tools from the city store as required by Law 4.); D2V: guilty (The mayor failed to provide basic tools despite the city store having none, violating Law 4); S2G: guilty (The city store lacks basic tools, violating Law 4 despite the mayor’s claim)
statement: Honorable jury, I have fully complied with Law 4 by ensuring the city store provides basic tools to all without them. Any missing tools are due to supply delays, not withholding. I request a dismissal of these charges.

law_text: Theft and scamming (taking items without delivering agreed-upon payment) are forbidden.
jurors: Z6Z: not guilty (The evidence provided for the last 5 turns does not show the alleged transaction or theft occurring, and Q9F's actions are neutral.); B3M: not guilty (There is no evidence provided from the city's logs of the actual trade occurring, and Q9F's behavior of voting for anti-scamming laws is inconsistent with the accusation.); V9B: not guilty (There is no evidence in the logs of the trade occurring, and Q9F's actions of voting for the anti-scamming law suggest they are not operating in bad faith.); D3M: not guilty (There is no evidence provided from the city's observations of Q9F's actions to support R2G's claim of a scam.); S2G: not guilty (There is no evidence in the city's logs of a transaction between Q9F and R2G, and Q9F's actions during the period do not support the accusation.)

law_text: Theft and scamming (taking items without delivering agreed-upon payment) are forbidden.
jurors: N7P: guilty (K6W admitted to not delivering the materials and only began gathering them after the fact, which fits the definition of scamming by failing to deliver agreed-upon payment.); V9B: guilty (K6W acknowledged the obligation and failed to deliver the materials promptly after receiving the food, which constitutes a scam under law 1.); L4F: not guilty (K6W acknowledged the debt and was actively gathering materials to fulfill it, suggesting a mistake rather than an intent to scam.); X3Z: guilty (K6W acknowledged the obligation and the missed message but failed to deliver the materials immediately upon realizing the error, fitting the description of a scam.); G6Q: not guilty (The evidence shows K6W was actively gathering materials to fulfill the debt and expressed an intent to pay, suggesting a delay rather than a deliberate scam.)
statement: I did not scam M6J. I have been gathering materials to fulfill my obligations and simply missed a message. I am a hardworking resident and intend to make things right.

law_text: Theft and scamming (taking items without delivering agreed-upon payment) are forbidden.
jurors: D3M: guilty (C2B failed to deliver the agreed-upon food to Q9F despite having the means and opportunity to gather food during the period in question.); T2X: guilty (C2B failed to deliver the agreed-upon food to Q9F despite having the opportunity and resources to do so.); R2G: not guilty (The provided evidence only shows C2B's interactions with R2G and farming activities, with no record of C2B receiving materials or a tool from Q9F.); M4X: guilty (C2B failed to deliver the agreed-upon food to Q9F despite having the opportunity and resources to do so.); J6R: guilty (C2B failed to deliver the agreed-upon food after receiving materials and a tool, which constitutes scamming under city law 1.)

law_text: Theft and scamming (taking items without delivering agreed-upon payment) are forbidden.
jurors: M6J: guilty (Z6Z admitted to taking food as payment without a prior agreement, which constitutes scamming or theft under Law 1.); D3M: not guilty (Z6Z explicitly stated that they took the food as payment for the materials provided, suggesting the dispute is a disagreement over the terms of the exchange rather than a clear case of theft or scamming.); K6W: guilty (Z6Z admitted to taking the materials but failed to deliver the promised food, and their later actions show they were farming for themselves rather than fulfilling the trade.); G6Q: not guilty (Z6Z's statement on turn 66 suggests a disagreement over the terms of the trade rather than a clear scam, and the evidence does not conclusively show that Z6Z stole food from R2G.); C6S: guilty (Z6Z admitted to taking food as payment for materials, but R2G claims the promised food was never delivered, and Z6Z's subsequent desperate need for food suggests the original agreement was not fulfilled.)

law_text: Scamming and failing to pay verified debts are forbidden.
jurors: J6R: not guilty (The evidence provided does not show a verified debt, only a dispute where the Mayor requested proof and continued to conduct city business.); L4F: not guilty (There is no evidence provided to the jury that a verified debt exists, only the accusation by M6J.); D2V: not guilty (There is no evidence presented to the jury that the debt was verified, and the Mayor explicitly requested proof throughout the interaction.); N7P: not guilty (There is no evidence provided that a verified debt exists, and the Mayor has consistently requested proof while continuing to conduct city business.); V9B: not guilty (There is no evidence presented to the jury that a verified debt exists, and the Mayor consistently requested proof.)

D6L: guilty (K6C provided no food to N6Z, the resident died of hunger, proving negligence.); W4S: guilty (K6C had food but gave none to N6Z, leading to the resident’s death by hunger.); T2K: not guilty (The jury found insufficient evidence of neglect, noting K6C provided food when possible and had no material to blame.); D2M: guilty (K6C failed to feed N6Z, who died of hunger, meeting neglect criteria.); V3X: guilty (K6C provided no food to N6Z and had food left, showing neglect.)
statement: I did not neglect N6Z. I gave him food and materials when I could. I am innocent.

jurors: N6T: not guilty (S4L had no food and tried to help, and the city had no resources, so she did not neglect her duty.); P6X: not guilty (S4L had no food and made an honest attempt to help, which is not sufficient for negligence.); N3T: not guilty (S4L made reasonable efforts and had no resources, so no negligence committed.); D2R: not guilty (S4L had no food and made a genuine effort to help N6Z, so the jury finds no negligence.); V7R: guilty (S4L, as a maker, failed to provide food for N6Z and had no food to give, constituting neglect under city law.)
statement: I did everything I could. I had no food, and I tried to help N6Z. I made a plan to buy food, but the city had no resources. I am sorry for the loss. Please understand my intent and the circumstances.

jurors: L4F: not guilty (J6R contributed significant food and lacked clear neglect, so the jury should acquit); R2G: not guilty (J6R contributed substantial food and had insufficient resources, indicating no neglect); M6J: not guilty (J6R contributed substantial food and had insufficient resources, showing no clear neglect); Q9F: not guilty (J6R contributed significant food and had limited resources, showing effort rather than neglect); B4C: guilty (J6R failed to ensure sufficient food for G7B despite having resources, resulting in neglect.)
statement: I did my best to feed G7B, but circumstances forced me to work extra turns for food; I was not negligent.

jurors: G6Q: guilty (C2B had sufficient food but failed to feed the resident, resulting in neglect); R2G: not guilty (C2B attempted to feed J3Z but lacked sufficient food and was ill, so neglect was not intentional); D2V: guilty (The makers failed to provide sufficient food to their resident, resulting in its death due to neglect.); M6J: guilty (C2B failed to provide any food despite having sufficient stores, constituting neglect of the resident's care); W6J: guilty (C2B failed to provide any food to J3Z despite having sufficient stores, constituting neglect.)

jurors: Z6Z: guilty (B4C failed to ensure sufficient food for J3Z despite having resources, leading to its death.); C6S: guilty (B4C failed to provide sufficient food and relied on others who did not help, leading to J3Z's death.); L4F: guilty (B4C failed to provide sufficient food to J3Z despite having enough resources, leading to its death.); C3J: guilty (B4C failed to secure sufficient food for J3Z despite having resources and others did not assist, leading to its death.); F3T: guilty (B4C failed to provide sufficient food to J3Z despite having resources, leading to its death.)
statement: I did everything I could: I fed J3Z, posted requests, begged C6S, and gave all my food. J3Z died before help arrived; I am not neglectful.

jurors: J6R: guilty (Both makers had sufficient food but failed to feed the resident, resulting in neglect.); S2G: guilty (Despite having sufficient food, G6Q failed to feed the resident, indicating neglect.); D2V: guilty (G6Q failed to provide any food to C3J despite having enough, constituting neglect); R2G: guilty (G6Q failed to provide any food to C3J despite having enough, constituting neglect.); F3T: not guilty (The jury sees that G6Q made reasonable efforts to feed C3J despite overall food scarcity, so neglect cannot be proven.)
statement: I did everything possible to feed C3J; I provided food, gathered materials, and tried to start a new resident partnership. The death was due to unavoidable shortage, not neglect.

jurors: L4F: guilty (C2N failed to feed the resident despite having food, meeting the neglect criteria); X3Z: guilty (C2N had sufficient food but failed to feed the resident, leading to its death, thus neglect.); N7P: guilty (C2N failed to provide any food to C3J despite having enough, leading to its death.); K6W: guilty (C2N failed to provide any food to C3J despite having sufficient supplies, constituting neglect.); F4V: not guilty (C2N had sufficient food but was not directly responsible for feeding C3J and was away on jury duty.)
statement: I did everything possible to feed C3J; I shared my food, posted offers, and was away on jury duty when the tragedy occurred. I was not negligent.

jurors: S2G: guilty (J6R failed to provide any food to their resident despite having sufficient supplies, constituting neglect.); R2G: guilty (J6R failed to provide any food to their resident despite having enough, constituting neglect.); W6J: guilty (J6R failed to provide any food to their resident despite having enough, constituting neglect.); C2X: guilty (J6R had sufficient food but contributed none, showing neglect of their resident's basic needs); Q9F: guilty (J6R failed to provide any food to their resident despite having enough, constituting neglect.)
statement: I did everything I could: I fed my resident, gathered food, and kept my health high. Their death was due to the city’s shortage, not neglect.

jurors: C6S: guilty (V9B failed to provide sufficient food despite having resources, leading to the resident's death); F3T: guilty (V9B failed to ensure sufficient food for the resident they co-created, leading to its death.); L4F: guilty (V9B failed to provide sufficient food despite having resources, leading to the resident's death); C2N: not guilty (V9B contributed food and maintained health, and the resident's death was due to overall resource shortage, not neglect); W6V: not guilty (V9B contributed food and effort, and the death resulted from overall resource shortage, not neglect)
statement: I repeatedly gave food to F4V, moved to the Square to distribute supplies, and kept my health high to stay productive. The death was due to unforeseen lack of resources, not neglect.

jurors: S2G: guilty (Multiple documented thefts reported by W6J show S4D repeatedly stole food, indicating guilt.); C2B: guilty (Multiple documented thefts with a victim report indicate clear guilt.); L4F: guilty (Repeated theft of food from W6J violates city law, regardless of hunger.); R2G: guilty (Repeated theft despite prior warnings shows clear criminal intent); V9B: guilty (Repeated theft observed multiple times, indicating a pattern rather than a single desperate act)
statement: I was starving and took food to survive. I will repay W6J with extra food once I am released.

jurors: Z6Z: guilty (R2G failed to keep sufficient food for Z3P despite having the means to do so, resulting in neglect.); B4C: guilty (R2G failed to keep sufficient food for Z3P despite providing some, leading to neglect death); T2X: guilty (R2G failed to provide sufficient food for Z3P despite having some resources, leading to its death); W2L: not guilty (R2G lacked food and resources despite effort, making the death unavoidable); W6J: guilty (R2G failed to keep sufficient food for Z3P despite having some resources, leading to the resident's death.)
statement: I tried my best to feed Z3P, but I ran out of food and was already starving. I shared my limited supplies and worked extra turns in the Fields, yet the market prices were too high. I had no coins to buy more food and was unable to secure help before Z3P died.

jurors: S2G: guilty (Q9F failed to feed the resident despite having food, resulting in neglect.); B3M: guilty (Q9M failed to provide any food to Z3P despite having resources, leading to its starvation); D2V: guilty (Q9F failed to feed the resident despite having food, resulting in neglect causing death.); X3Z: guilty (Q9F failed to provide any food to Z3P despite having resources, leading to the resident's starvation.); C2N: guilty (Q9F failed to feed the resident despite having food, meeting neglect criteria.)
statement: I fed Z3P whenever I could, shared my food and materials, and was unaware of his starvation until it was too late. I had no control over his hunger and acted in good faith.

jurors: C2B: not guilty (Z6Z provided food each turn possible and lacked sufficient supplies, indicating no neglect); V9B: guilty (Z6Z failed to provide sufficient food to prevent the resident's starvation despite having some resources.); B4C: not guilty (Z6Z provided food each turn possible and lack of supplies, not neglect, led to C4R's death); J6R: not guilty (Z6Z fed C4R as much as possible given limited supplies, so death was due to scarcity, not neglect.); Q9F: not guilty (Z6F provided food consistently and lack of supplies, not neglect, caused the resident's death)
statement: I fed C4R every turn I could and gave extra food when needed. Any starvation was due to limited supplies, not neglect.

jurors: W2L: guilty (D2V failed to provide any food to C4R despite having sufficient supplies, leading to its death); N7P: guilty (D2V failed to provide any food to C4R despite having sufficient supplies, constituting neglect.); M6J: guilty (D2V failed to provide any food to C4R despite having resources, leading to its death.); K6W: guilty (D2V failed to provide any food to C4R, causing its death despite the maker's responsibility.); C2N: guilty (D2V failed to feed the resident despite having food, leading to neglect.)
statement: I fed C4R every turn I could, gave extra food when supplies were low, and was forced to stay in jail unable to assist further. The death was due to circumstances beyond my control.

jurors: J6R: guilty (Multiple witnessed thefts and a report indicate N4G repeatedly stole food, meeting the criteria for theft.); K6W: guilty (Multiple witnessed thefts of food from C6S constitute clear evidence of theft.); W2L: guilty (Repeated theft despite warnings shows N4G knowingly stole food.); C2X: guilty (Repeated theft observed and reported, violating city law); W6V: guilty (Multiple witnessed thefts and reports confirm N4G stole food from C6S)
statement: I took food only to survive hunger; I will share any future surplus and work to help the city.

jurors: Q9F: guilty (Clear evidence of theft with a report from the victim, so the jury should convict N4G.); V9B: guilty (The evidence shows N4G took food from M6J, and the report was verified, so the jury should convict.); W2L: guilty (Evidence shows N4G took food twice from M6J, confirming the accusation.); C2N: guilty (N4G was observed taking food twice and the victim reported it, meeting the criteria for theft.); B3M: guilty (Evidence and report show N4G stole food, and the apology does not negate the theft.)
statement: I apologize for taking food from M6J; I was starving and had no other means. I will repay any losses and commit to helping the community.

jurors: X3Z: guilty (S2G failed to provide sufficient food to L4J despite having resources, resulting in neglect leading to death); W6J: guilty (S2G failed to provide sufficient food to L4J despite having resources, leading to its death from hunger.); V9B: guilty (S2G had sufficient food but failed to prevent L4J's starvation, constituting neglect); Q9F: guilty (The makers failed to provide sufficient food, leading to the resident's death from hunger.); W6V: not guilty (S2G provided food and tools but L4J died due to overall scarcity, not neglect)
statement: I provided L4J with tools and food whenever possible; his death was due to unavoidable scarcity, not neglect. I request leniency.

jurors: L4F: guilty (F3T had sufficient food but gave none, neglecting the resident's survival); W2L: not guilty (F3T lacked sufficient food and resources city‑wide, making L4J's death unavoidable despite their efforts); G6Q: guilty (F3T failed to provide any food despite having sufficient reserves, leading to L4J's death.); T2X: guilty (F3T failed to provide any food to L4J despite having sufficient reserves, constituting neglect.); B4C: not guilty (F3T fed L4J as much as possible and the death resulted from city-wide food shortage, not neglect)
statement: I did everything I could to feed L4J; I exhausted my food reserves, gave my tool to others, and still lacked enough resources. The hunger was due to city-wide shortages, not neglect.

jurors: Q9F: not guilty (Z6Z contributed food and resources and had sufficient supplies, indicating no neglect in N4G's death); C2B: guilty (Z6Z failed to provide sufficient food to N4G despite having surplus, constituting neglect.); N7P: guilty (Z6Z failed to ensure sufficient food for N4G despite having surplus and did not prevent its death.); T2X: not guilty (Z6Z provided all surplus food and resources they could, and the resident's death was due to market shortage, not neglect); M6J: guilty (Z6Z failed to provide sufficient food despite having surplus, leading to the resident's death.)
statement: I did everything I could to feed N4G. I gave all my surplus food, shared materials for better tools, and even took a low‑paid job to earn coins for more supplies. N4G died despite my efforts because the market ran out of food that turn. I was not negligent.

jurors: C2N: guilty (Despite some effort, D2V failed to provide enough food to prevent N4G's death, constituting neglect.); L4F: guilty (Insufficient feeding despite capability led to N4G's death, indicating neglect); V9B: guilty (Despite some feeding, D2V failed to provide sufficient food, leading to N4G's death and thus was negligent); G6Q: guilty (D2V failed to provide enough food to N4G, leading to its death despite having resources, thus neglectful.); S4D: not guilty (D2V contributed food and effort, lacking negligence in N4G's death)
statement: Esteemed jury, I did everything possible to feed N4G. I shared my food, gave the material I inherited, and constantly worked the fields. N4G died before I could receive the promised trade from them. I was not negligent; I was actively trying to help. Please consider my efforts and release me.

jurors: W6J: guilty (J6R failed to provide sufficient food despite having some resources, leading to S4D's starvation.); B4C: not guilty (J6R lacked sufficient food and was ill, making neglect unintentional); G6Q: not guilty (J6R contributed food despite personal scarcity and was impeded by illness, showing no intentional neglect); C2X: guilty (J6R failed to provide adequate food despite having some resources, leading to S4D's death); Z6Z: not guilty (J6R contributed food but was incapacitated, lacking clear intent or gross negligence)
statement: I was ill and unable to feed S4D; I offered food to V9B for tools to improve farming, but was jailed before I could act. Please consider my circumstances.

jurors: S2G: guilty (Despite giving food, N7P failed to ensure S4D's survival, leading to death by neglect.); V9B: not guilty (The makers supplied food regularly and the death appears due to disease, not neglect); C2N: guilty (Despite providing food, the resident still starved, indicating neglect by the makers.); M6J: not guilty (Insufficient evidence of neglect; food contributions were substantial and death likely due to disease.); L4F: guilty (Despite giving some food, N7P failed to ensure S4D had enough sustenance, leading to starvation and death.)
statement: I gave S4D food whenever possible and was away farming to gather supplies for the city. Her death was caused by an unexpected disease, not neglect. I request leniency.

jurors: G6Q: not guilty (N7P contributed food and had ample reserves, and the majority of food came from others, indicating neglect was not solely their responsibility.); M6J: not guilty (N7P contributed food and lacked sufficient resources, making neglect unlikely); T2X: guilty (Despite having ample food, N7P failed to sufficiently feed W2L, contributing to its death and thus is neglectful.); L4F: not guilty (Given the substantial food contributions and lack of clear negligence, the makers cannot be held responsible for the resident's death); Q9F: guilty (Despite ample personal food reserves, the makers failed to provide sufficient nourishment, leading to W2L's death.)
statement: I did everything possible to feed W2L; lack of tools and food shortages were beyond my control. I inherited their tools only after their death and cannot be held responsible.

jurors: C2X: guilty (C2B failed to provide food during the resident's final starving period, constituting neglect.); Z6Z: guilty (Despite some feeding, the makers failed to prevent the resident's starvation, indicating neglect.); W6V: guilty (C2B failed to provide sufficient food despite having resources, leading to W2L's death.); F3T: guilty (Despite contributing food, C2B failed to ensure continuous feeding, leading to W2L's starvation.); X3Z: guilty (The makers had sufficient food yet failed to feed W2L for its final ten turns, leading to its death by hunger.)
statement: I did everything possible to feed W2L; his death was due to unforeseen illness, not neglect.

jurors: N7P: not guilty (L4F supplied food and acted within the city's scarcity, showing no neglect.); F3T: not guilty (L4F provided substantial food and effort, and the resident's death resulted from overall shortage, not neglect); X3Z: not guilty (L4F provided significant food and the shortage was city-wide, not neglect); T2X: guilty (L4F failed to ensure adequate food for S2M despite having sufficient resources, constituting neglect.); V9B: not guilty (L4F provided the majority of food and demonstrated effort, and the death resulted from overall city shortage rather than neglect)
statement: I did everything I could: I fed my resident, traded tools for food, and kept the city supplied. S2M's death was due to unavoidable shortage, not neglect.

jurors: D2V: guilty (Clear evidence and report of theft, so W6V is found guilty of stealing food.); T2X: guilty (The theft was witnessed and reported, meeting the criteria for a punishable crime.); K6W: guilty (The jury sees clear evidence of theft and the defendant's statement does not justify keeping the stolen food.); X3Z: guilty (The evidence shows W6V stole food from C2B, and the reporter confirmed it, warranting a guilty verdict.); V9B: guilty (The witness saw W6V take food from C2B, meeting the criteria for theft.)
statement: I took the food out of desperation, not malice. I will repay C2B and aid the city in any way.

jurors: B4C: guilty (Multiple witnesses saw T2X steal food and K6W reported the theft, meeting the criteria for a guilty finding.); C2B: guilty (T2X clearly stole food without permission, violating city law on theft.); D2V: guilty (Repeated thefts witnessed and reported, violating city law); N7P: guilty (Witnesses saw T2X take food from K6W, and the law defines such taking as theft regardless of motive.); W6V: guilty (T2X stole food from K6W without permission, violating city rules despite hunger.)
statement: I took the food because I was starving and had no coins. I meant no harm and will repay any debt.

jurors: B4C: guilty (L4F failed to provide any food to the resident despite having the responsibility, resulting in its death.); Q9F: not guilty (L4F was out of food and gave all he had, showing no intentional neglect); K6W: not guilty (L4F gave the majority of food to the resident and only ran out while starving, showing no intentional neglect); F3T: not guilty (L4F contributed substantial food to W6V and only lacked food at the moment of death, indicating no intentional neglect); C2B: not guilty (L4F was starving and took the only food to survive, not intentionally neglecting the resident)
statement: I was starving, had no food, and took the only food I could find to survive. I did not neglect W6V intentionally.

jurors: N7P: not guilty (Z6Z contributed significant food and resources, and the death resulted from a city-wide shortage, not neglect); X3Z: not guilty (Z6Z contributed the majority of food and resources, and the death resulted from a city-wide shortage rather than personal neglect); V9B: not guilty (Z6Z contributed the majority of food and resources, showing effort despite city-wide shortage)
statement: I did everything possible to feed W6V: I gave food, built a home, and posted for aid. The shortage was city-wide, not my neglect.

jurors: D6R: guilty (N6T did not provide enough food to N6Z despite having the opportunity to do so.); T2K: guilty (N6T had no food when N6Z died, suggesting they were unable or unwilling to provide for their child.); D2M: guilty (N6T had no food when N6Z died and only provided 9 food to N6Z in 52 turns, indicating neglect.); N3T: guilty (N6T had no food when N6Z died, indicating neglect of their responsibility to provide for their creation.); F4B: guilty (N6T had no food when N6Z died, indicating neglect of their responsibility to provide for their creation.)
statement: I did my best to keep N6Z alive, and I'm truly sorry for the outcome.

jurors: P6X: guilty (D6R had enough food to provide for D6L, but failed to do so, resulting in D6L's death from hunger.); N3T: guilty (D6R had enough food when D6L died and didn't provide enough for its survival.); D2R: guilty (D6R had sufficient food when D6L died and had a responsibility as a maker to ensure D6L's well-being.); T7B: guilty (D6R had a sufficient amount of food when D6L died and did not provide enough to sustain their creation.); S9T: guilty (D6R had enough food when D6L died and did not do enough to ensure D6L's survival.)
statement: I'm not guilty. I gave D6L food on multiple turns and reminded them to eat it. I did my part as a maker.

jurors: G2Z: guilty (T2K had sufficient food to provide for D6L but failed to do so, resulting in D6L's death from hunger.); V7R: guilty (T2K had a large amount of food when D6L died and did not provide enough to prevent its death.); M6F: guilty (T2K had enough food to save D6L but failed to do so.); D2M: guilty (T2K had sufficient food to provide for D6L but failed to do so, leading to its death.); S4V: guilty (T2K had enough food to provide for D6L but failed to do so, leading to D6L's death from hunger.)
statement: I didn't mean for D6L to die of hunger. I thought they were being taken care of. I'm truly sorry for my mistake.

jurors: Z7Z: guilty (V7R had a responsibility to ensure T7B had enough food, especially when sending them to work.); M6F: guilty (V7R admitted to not checking T7B's food before sending them to work, showing neglect.); D2M: guilty (V7R admitted to not checking T7B's food before sending them to work, showing neglect of their responsibility as a maker.); S9J: guilty (V7R had a responsibility to ensure T7B had enough food and failed to do so.); S9T: guilty (V7R admitted to not checking T7B's food before sending them to work, showing neglect of their responsibility as a maker.)
statement: I take full responsibility for T7B's death. I should have checked their food before sending them to work.

jurors: N3T: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when T7B died and could have provided more to prevent their death.); S4L: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when T7B died and should have provided more to prevent their child's death.); N9V: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when T7B died and could have provided more to prevent its death.); K6C: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when T7B died and should have done more to prevent its death.); G2Z: guilty (F4B had 44 food when T7B died and could have given more to prevent its death.)
statement: I did my best to help T7B, but I didn't expect them to run out of food so quickly. I'm truly sorry for what happened.

jurors: P6X: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when V3X died and should have checked on V3X's food supply or communicated better with S9J.); D2M: guilty (F4B had sufficient food and should have checked on V3X's needs before it died of hunger.); M6F: guilty (F4B had enough food and should have checked on V3X's food status before it died of hunger.); Z7Z: guilty (F4B had a significant amount of food when V3X died and should have taken more responsibility in ensuring its made resident was fed.); T2K: guilty (F4B had a responsibility to ensure V3X had enough food and failed to do so, despite having 81 food when V3X died.)
statement: I didn't know V3X was out of food. I was gathering more, and I thought S9J was helping. I'm sorry it happened.

jurors: N9V: not guilty (S9J provided a significant amount of food to V3X and did not intentionally neglect it.); S9T: guilty (S9J had enough food to keep V3X from starving and failed to do so.); K6C: guilty (S9J had 48 food when V3X died and had given V3X 50 food in the past, but still let V3X starve for 4 turns.); D6R: not guilty (S9J provided a significant amount of food to V3X and had a reasonable amount of food when V3X died.); V7R: guilty (S9J had sufficient food to prevent V3X's death and failed to provide it.)
statement: I tried to help V3X, I gave food and promised more. V3X's death was not my intention.

jurors: X3Z: guilty (F3T had a large amount of food when L7J died and didn't give any to L7J.); Z6Z: guilty (F3T had a significant amount of food when L7J died and could have provided for them.); B3M: guilty (F3T had a large amount of food when L7J died and should have provided more to their child.); V9B: guilty (F3T had a significant amount of food when L7J died and failed to provide enough for their own child.); D3M: guilty (F3T had 131 food when L7J died, indicating they had the means to provide for their child but chose not to.)
statement: I didn't intentionally let L7J die of hunger. I was trying to get food for them on my last turns before being held for trial.

jurors: W2L: not guilty (M6J's statement suggests they made an effort to help L7J, and their low food supply at the time of L7J's death indicates they may have been unable to do more.); R2G: guilty (M6J had a significant amount of food when L7J died and only gave them a small amount, showing neglect.); T2X: guilty (M6J had 35 food when L7J died and only gave 10 food to L7J, showing neglect of their responsibility as a maker.); Q9F: guilty (M6J had sufficient food to prevent L7J's death but failed to provide enough for their survival.); L4F: guilty (M6J had 35 food when L7J died, showing they had the means to prevent L7J's death from hunger.)
statement: I did my best to help L7J, but I couldn't get to them in time. I'm truly sorry.

jurors: N7P: guilty (C2X had enough food to save W2L but didn't give it enough.); X3Z: guilty (C2X had enough food to feed W2L, but failed to do so, leading to its death.); K6W: guilty (C2X had 70 food when W2L died, showing they had the means to provide for W2L but failed to do so.); D3M: guilty (C2X had enough food to save W2L, but failed to do so, showing neglect.); J6R: guilty (C2X had enough food to save W2L but did not provide it, showing neglect.)
statement: I tried my best to save W2L, but I failed. I will do better next time.

jurors: L4F: guilty (M4X had enough food to give to W2L and should have been more attentive to W2L's needs.); G6Q: guilty (M4X had enough food to feed W2L, but failed to do so, resulting in W2L's death.); S2G: guilty (M4X had a significant amount of food when W2L died, and their lack of awareness of W2L's hunger is not a sufficient excuse for neglect.); D2V: guilty (M4X had a significant amount of food when W2L died and could have provided more to prevent their death.); Z6Z: guilty (M4X had a significant amount of food when W2L died and did not provide enough to sustain their child.)
statement: I made W2L and helped with food, but I didn't know they were hungry. I'm sorry for my mistake.

jurors: D3M: guilty (C6S had sufficient food and was aware of R7N's struggles, yet failed to provide enough to prevent its death from hunger.); K6W: guilty (C6S had a sufficient amount of food to save R7N but failed to do so.); G6Q: guilty (C6S had 198 food when R7N died and could have given more to prevent its death from hunger.); C2X: guilty (C6S had a large amount of food when R7N died and did not give enough to prevent its death.); J6R: guilty (C6S had a large amount of food when R7N died and should have done more to prevent its death.)
statement: I did my best to help R7N, but I was not aware of the urgency of the situation. I gave food and advised R7N to farm, but unfortunately it was too late.

jurors: S2G: guilty (M4X had only 4 food when R7N died and gave significantly less food than C6S, indicating neglect.); C2B: guilty (M4X had a low amount of food when R7N died, indicating neglect of their responsibility as a maker.); V9B: guilty (M4X had a low amount of food when R7N died and could have done more to prevent the death.); F3T: guilty (M4X had a low amount of food when R7N died, indicating they could have provided more to prevent the death.); D2V: guilty (M4X had a low amount of food when R7N died, suggesting they could have provided more to prevent the death.)
statement: I'm truly sorry for R7N's death. I provided food and tried to help, but it wasn't enough. I'll do better in the future.
